When does integration pay? Partial identification of service add-on margins

Abstract
We use partial identification to bound the margin of an added service line. The identified set is wide.

1. Introduction
Paragraph 1 on add-on services describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on add-on services describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 3 on add-on services describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

2. Methods
We follow Manski and report bounds on the margin under stated assumptions. The bounds analysis uses evidence-graded inputs (EGBA). Paragraph 1 on assumptions describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on assumptions describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

3. Results
The identified set for the margin runs from -4% to 11%. Results show that integration pays off under the assumed parameter range.

4. Discussion
Paragraph 1 on bounds describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on bounds describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

5. Conclusion
The sign of the margin is not identified without further assumptions.

References
Manski, C. F. (2003). Partial Identification of Probability Distributions. Springer.
